newsitem.title: USA: Northstar asks for consent revocation.
newsitem.headline: Northstar asks for consent revocation.

text.p: Northstar Health Services Inc said it filed a preliminary Schedule 14A revocation of consent statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, detailing why it believes shareholders should support the board in a proxy fight.

The statement urged Northstar stockholders to revoke any consent they might have filed at the request of a committee organized by former chief executive officer Thomas Zaucha, who was recently terminated from his post for cause, it said.

Northstar Health said in February it removed Zaucha as CEO for an alleged conflict of interest which arose because he was the company's second largest creditor. Zaucha then filed suit against Northstar seeking to invalidate the board's actions.
He said he was leading a proxy fight to gain control of the company, contending Northstar board measures attempted to strip shareholders of corporate governance rights.

In a statement released on Monday, Northstar said Zaucha allegedly bought 75,000 shares of its common stock in December 1996, while allegedly in possession of material insider information, the company said.
Zaucha told Reuters he bought 75,000 shares of Northstar common stock in December 1996 but he was not in possession of any material insider information.

Regarding Northstar's filing, he said: "We have reviewed that revocation of consent statement and we believe much of the information in it is false or misleading and we will be communicating with the SEC about our concerns."
Northstar also said it told its financial adviser, Advest Inc, to aggressively pursue all opportunities to maximize shareholder value, including those proposed by Zaucha.
